newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia year-on-year CPI up 3.4 pct in October.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia year-on-year CPI up 3.4 pct in October.

text.p: Malaysia's Consumer Price Index (CPI) for October rose 3.4 percent from the same month a year ago, the Statistics Department said on Saturday.
In September 1996, the index grew by 3.6 percent on a year-on-year basis.
The index gained 3.5 percent for the first 10 months of this year compared with the corresponding period last year, the department said in a report.
The 10-month increase in the CPI, a measure of inflation at the retail level, resulted from index rises in all the main groups except for clothing and footwear, which fell by 0.8 percent.

The department said the CPI in October was unchanged from September 1996. Compared with September, the CPI for October 1996 was stable at 107.7 because increases in four main groups were offset by declines in three other groups and little change in two groups.

From September to October 1996, increases were seen in gross rent, fuel and power, transport and communication, miscellaneous goods and services, and medical care and health expenses, the department said.
